Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

private adjective and adverb

confidential

also in private, privately, confidential, secretly, between ourselves, I want to speak with you privately, in secret, tell a secret

classical

Quint. 2.18.4: ex sēcrētīs studiīs (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 7.9.4 (Lewis & Short)

sēcrētus, sēcrēta, sēcrētum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

private, secret

Set apart, and so private or secret (Lewis & Short). As a noun, sēcrētum is a secret or a private talk: sēcrētum petit, he asks for a word in private (Plin. Ep. 1.5.11, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • sēcrētō — in private, privately

    adverb · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.25.2; Hor. S. 1.9.67 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 365 · Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: in secret, without witnesses, in private. Traupman: velim tēcum loquī sēcrētō, I want to speak with you privately.

  • in prīvātō — in private, not in public

    phrase: in with the ablative · also used · classical · Liv. 39.18 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 91, 365; Traupman 106: I want to speak with you privately, velim tēcum loquī in prīvātō

    Against in pūblicō, in public (Lewis & Short).

  • in sēcrētō — in private, secretly

    also used · classical · Liv. 26.19.5: tempus in sēcrētō ibi tereret (Lewis & Short s.v. sēcernō); Traupman 106: privately, in sēcrētō

Examples

  • Sēcrētō hoc audī, tēcum habētō, nē Apellae quidem, lībertō tuō, dīxerīs.

    This is between ourselves: keep it to yourself, and don’t tell even your freedman Apella.Cic. Fam. 7.25.2

  • Mālim tēcum dē eā in prīvātō loquī.

    I’d rather talk to you about that in private.Traupman 91

  • Velim tēcum loquī in prīvātō.

    I’d like to speak with you privately.Traupman 106

  • sēcrētum ēloquī

    to tell a secretTraupman 392

See also private, talk, personal.
